title: The Missing Treaty Basis: Why the EU AI Act's Implementing Powers Are Constitutionally Defective
description: This article explains why key parts of the EU’s AI Act (Regulation 2024/1689) may be legally invalid. The Act gives the European Commission the power to adopt “implementing acts” and impose fines, but it never cites the Treaty article (Article 291 TFEU) required to grant those powers. Without that legal basis, the Commission's actions could be challenged and annulled in court. The Act also claims to give the Commission exclusive enforcement authority, bypassing Member States and creating an internal “AI Office” with powers the Treaties don’t allow. This breaches basic EU constitutional principles like conferral of powers, rule of law, and institutional balance. If left unchallenged, the AI Act sets a dangerous precedent: letting EU institutions assume powers they were never given.
